P1.evidence: P1a miss — nothing from the application or setter notes was read back, and the tell is that the rep did not learn until 00:21:47 that the girlfriend was the one who made contact ('Actually, was my girlfriend that got in touch with you guys'). That is a fact any set of notes would have carried, and it turned out to be the single most important commercial fact on the call. P1b partial — three of four parts: 'I want to get a quick picture of where you're at right now. I just want to understand what's going on, what have you tried, and where you're trying to get to.' 'What you need' was never framed. He did add a good takeaway close on the frame — 'if not, no worries, we'll just shake hands and part as friends.' P1c hit — agreement was explicitly requested and given: 'Sounds good?' / 'Sounds good.' P1d hit — clean open question: 'So walk me through briefly, what's the main thing you're looking to fix right now?'

P2.evidence: The best-executed baseline in this batch, with one indefensible hole. P2a miss — age, height and weight were never asked, on a call with a cancer patient where body weight is a clinically monitored variable and where he himself raised chemo-driven weight loss ('they would become like 25 kilos or whatever'). P2b hit — 'do you work right now or what does it look like?' P2c partial — the rep followed the volunteered diagnosis thoroughly, asking radiation frequency, total sessions, remaining duration, the chemo timeline and whether the supplements were prescribed, but never ran a general health or hereditary screen and, critically, never asked whether any clinician had cleared him to train. P2d hit — asked directly and correctly separated injury from stiffness: 'But do you have, like, any injuries, or these are just, like, stiffness from all the...' P2e hit — 'do you regularly work out with strength conditioning?', then confirmed the actual number, three times a week. P2f miss — never asked what results the current training is producing. P2g hit — strongest questioning of the call: 'And what does it look like in terms of nutrition right now for you?', then 'How long have you been on a keto diet?', then 'And how do you find that? Like, is it easy for you?' P2h miss — sleep was volunteered ('I'm sleeping a little bit more because of the radiation') and never asked about; quantity and quality were never established for a man in daily radiotherapy. P2i hit — asked twice and pinned down a number: 'your overall energy levels, is that affecting in any way?' produced '75% of energy'.

P3.evidence: P3a hit — the magic-wand question ran properly: 'if you could have like a magic wand to solve this tomorrow, what would be the biggest relief... Or, like, what becomes possible afterward?' P3b hit — the rep reflected the axes back accurately and got confirmation: 'you basically want to get more mobility, gain strength, and get rid of the stiffness of the back and hips.' P3c miss — never asked what he wants to do physically but can't; the answer was sitting there in the back pain that follows his sessions. P3d hit — the magic-wand question was the bridge and it worked, taking him straight past the physical to 'the main thing of being diagnosed with that is, like, people around you, the people that love you.' P3e partial — never asked what moving better would actually do for him; Bruno supplied it himself ('if I'm feeling fit, if I'm feeling stronger, I'm more likely to go to the treatment well'). P3f partial — the rep asserted the impact-on-others rather than asking it: 'it's not only for you, but it's also for the others that are for your close ones, yeah?' P3g partial — the deepest material in the batch was on the table unprompted, including mortality, a three-to-five-year prognosis and the suffering of the people around him, and the rep acknowledged it and moved on ('for me, it's pretty simple... you have the strongest why') rather than driving through it. Understandable humanly; still not the phase being run. P3h hit — the reflect-back landed well: 'So it's not only about like getting fit, like the most of guys that I talk to. It's actually about... getting you in a best position for a fight.'

P4.evidence: Skipped almost entirely. P4a partial — 'what have you tried' appeared once inside the opening frame and was never returned to. P4b, P4c, P4d, P4e all miss — no question about what happened with previous efforts, why they did not stick, what is actually in the way, and no invitation to name his own gap. He named it anyway, unprompted: 'rather than plan for a gym, that I wouldn't be as motivated to do it', and separately 'Before, I was a little bit lazy. I would do maybe once, twice a week.' Both were left on the floor. P4f miss — and this was the most conspicuous open goal in the batch: the prospect is a professional coach. 'You coach people for a living. Why can't you coach yourself?' writes itself, and would have made the accountability pillar inevitable. The rep gestured at it only in the pitch ('you're a coach, so you probably understand how coaching important is') rather than using it as a question in discovery.

P5.evidence: Not run at all. No two-year question, no settling question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. It should be recorded, though, that this is the one call in the batch where skipping Phase 5 may have been the right human call: the scripted consequence frame asks a man with an aggressive brain cancer and a quoted three-to-five-year prognosis to imagine what life looks like if nothing changes, and running it as written would have been ugly. The rep instead pointed the same energy at the positive frame — 'you have the strongest why you need to do it out of all of the guys that I've ever spoke to.' Scored a miss because the process was demonstrably not run, but flagged for the process owner rather than for the rep: the playbook has no guidance for what the consequence frame becomes when the consequence is already terminal.

P6.evidence: The best-run phase in the batch, and it was run in the right order — before any price was named. P6a hit, close to verbatim: 'just to make sure that we are on the same page, if you have the right training, the simple nutrition, and Trevor in your corner, like, do you agree that you would actually get to your goal of feeling better and getting through this difficult time that you're going to encounter?' Answer: 'A hundred percent, yeah. A hundred percent.' P6b hit — the go-all-in ask followed immediately: 'if we can figure out the details, like, are you sure you want to commit to this and become the version 2.0 of Bruno that kicks the [expletive] of the cancer?' Answer: 'Yeah, 100%. That's what I'm looking for. That's for sure. So, let's do it.' Slightly weaker than the script in that he never asked whether there was any reason not to go all in, which would have surfaced the girlfriend and the finances before the number rather than after. P6c partial — the yes was clear and correctly obtained before presenting, but when hesitation surfaced on price the rep did not return to Phase 5 as instructed; he went to logistics and then to a follow-up.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — both tiers were priced and the rep asked 'Which one are you leaning towards?' — but no agreement to pay was obtained, so payment collection, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome-email walkthrough were all unreachable on this call. Scored N/A rather than miss so the phase does not double-count the unresolved money objection.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger explicit: 'I just need to check with my girlfriend.' The rep opened correctly with the money-aside isolation — 'money aside, like, do you personally feel that this can get you [there]?' — and it produced the strongest value statement of the call: '100% have someone to coach me... It would be huge, because then I have guidance.' He then made a good unscripted move, asking her to join live: 'Can you get her on a call right now? We can talk right now.' That is the right instinct and it deserves credit. Everything after that stopped. Not run: 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up' (which would have surfaced the unknown chemo costs before they became the reason), 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', and the deposit-plus-full-refund fallback, which is precisely the structure this situation called for. Note one scripted move that should NOT have been run and correctly was not: 'is this genuinely needing her input, or asking permission to bet on yourself' would have been wrong here, because she demonstrably controls the accounts — 'she's the one that takes care of the bills' — and she is the one who sought Primal out in the first place. She is a decision-maker, not a permission gate, and the play does not distinguish the two.

Two moves run well, then the play collapsed. The should-versus-how reframe was executed almost to the letter: 'So we're talking purely logistics, not like, should I do it, but actually how to do it in terms of finances?' The payment-plan door was opened: 'there are ways that we can move around with finances. If the payment in one installment is difficult, we can work around and maybe split it.' Then the rep inverted the play — 'But I would need to know from you what level of investments you can commit to at the beginning' — which asks the prospect to price himself instead of the rep discovering the picture. The financial picture was never taken: one abandoned question ('do you want to check, like, your checking account? Like, how much do you have?') and then nothing. Not asked: what is left over each month after bills, how many credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, crypto/stocks/investments. Worst of all, when the prospect asked directly for something concrete — 'if you can send me maybe a few options of how can we pay it or if there is payment plan' — the answer was 'we don't have, like, a set payment plans.' The one artifact that could have moved this deal was requested and refused.

Soft trigger, and worth recording as soft: 'we are really keen. We just cannot give you an answer right now because we need to check the finances... So we're going to think.' No moves ran. In fairness this is closer to a genuine information-gathering delay than a stall — he needs actual balances from the person who holds them — so the full Objection A treatment would have been misapplied. But the two openers still had a place and were not used: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to [goal]?' had already been answered yes, and 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?' would have cost nothing.

SCRIPT GAP — clinical fit, in the most serious form the corpus has produced. The prospect is eight weeks post-craniotomy, at session 18 of 33 radiotherapy sessions, and beginning twelve months of chemotherapy in seven weeks. He is being sold six to twelve months of loaded ballistic kettlebell training. Nobody on either side of the call asked whether his oncologist, surgeon or physio has cleared him for it; the rep did not raise it and the playbook does not require it. This is the same gap already logged from the Tyron Giuliani call, but there the clinician had at least been consulted. Here the question was never asked at all. Compounding it: the prospect disclosed active distrust of his medical team — 'those doctors, when are you dead? So you've got to do a bit by yourself... They don't let me take anything' — and the rep affirmed the frame rather than treating it as a flag. A mandatory clearance question belongs in Phase 2 and does not currently exist.

SCRIPT GAP — an unbounded and unknowable competing financial obligation. Bruno's objection was not that he lacks money, it was that he cannot size the decision: 'the amount of money that we're going to have to pay for the chemo, we are not really sure yet of the exams, how often we're going to have to do blood tests. So it's hard to commit for, like, big investments when you have something like I do.' Objection C is built for a prospect whose finances are knowable and merely inconvenient; every one of its financial-picture questions assumes a fixed denominator. There is no move for a prospect facing a real, dated, open-ended liability. The obvious answers — a smaller first instalment, a start date deferred into the four-week gap before chemo, a refundable deposit to hold the price — are all available in principle and none is in the script. Worth building; this shape will recur with any prospect in active medical treatment.

SCRIPT GAP — the nutrition pillar has no handling for a therapeutic diet. Bruno is eight weeks into strict keto as part of his cancer strategy. The rep delivered the standard pillar including the weekly balance day: 'once a week, you're going to have like a, quote unquote, like a day off. It's not a cheat meal... But you can have a pizza or something like that, just for mind's sound.' That breaks ketosis, and it was offered to a man whose diet is a deliberate part of an oncology protocol. He accepted it without objection, which means nothing corrected it. The pillar script needs a branch that recognises a medically motivated diet and holds it fixed rather than layering the standard structure over it.

notes: Two genuinely strong phases — the baseline questioning (P2) and, unusually for this batch, a properly sequenced commitment check (P6) taken before any price was named — sitting either side of a root-cause phase that was not run at all. The commercial failure is narrow and fixable: the money objection was isolated correctly and then abandoned at the exact point the play gets useful, and the prospect's direct request for written payment options was declined, so the person who actually controls the money received nothing to look at. For the follow-up: bring a costed instalment structure, propose a start date in the four-week window between radiotherapy and chemo, and get the girlfriend on the call, since she initiated the enquiry and holds the accounts. Separately, and above the sales coaching: this call needs a policy decision, not a coaching note. There is no clinical clearance step anywhere in the process, and the rep sold six to twelve months of loaded kettlebell work to a man mid-radiotherapy for aggressive brain cancer without anyone asking a doctor. The playbook also has no answer for what the consequence frame becomes when the consequence is a terminal prognosis, and the rep was left to improvise 'version 2.0 of Bruno that kicks the [expletive] of the cancer' on his own.
